ety.text: Inherited from Middle English orbite, orbita, from Latin orbita (“course, track, impression, mark”).

senses.d: An elliptical movement of an object about a celestial object or Lagrange point, especially a periodic elliptical revolution.
One complete circuit round an orbited body.
ex: The Moon's orbit around the Earth takes nearly one month to complete.

senses.d: The state of moving in an orbit.
The path of an electron around an atomic nucleus.
A path for the ball on the outer edge of the playfield, usually connected so that the ball entering in one end will come out of the other.
A sphere of influence; an area or extent of activity, interest, or control.
ex: In the post WWII era, several eastern European countries came into the orbit of the Soviet Union.
The convenience store was a heavily travelled point in her daily orbit, as she purchased both cigarettes and lottery tickets there.

senses.d: The bony cavity in the skull of a vertebrate containing the eyeball.
The area around the eye of a bird or other animal.
A collection of points related by the evolution function of a dynamical system.
The subset of elements of a set X to which a given element can be moved by members of a specified group of transformations that act on X.
To circle or revolve around another object or position.
ex: The satellite orbits the Lagrange point.

senses.d: To place an object (e.g. a satellite) into an orbit around a planet.
ex: A rocket was used to orbit the satellite.

senses.d: To move around the general vicinity of something.
ex: The harried mother had a cloud of children orbiting her, begging for sweets.

senses.d: To move in a circle.
To center (around).
ex: I have orbited my entire life around you, and you know it, okay?

senses.d: To continue to follow or engage with someone by means of social media after breaking up with them.

Borrowed from Medieval Latin orbitālis, from orbita (“a track or rut; a circuit, orbit”) + -ālis (“-al”, adjectival suffix), equivalent to orbit + -al. Doublet of orbitalis.

senses.d: Of or relating to, or forming an orbit (such as the orbit of a moon, planet, or spacecraft).
Of or relating to the eye socket (eyehole).
(of roads, railways) Passing around the outside of an urban area.
ex: The M25 is an orbital motorway around London.

senses.d: A specification of the energy and probability density of one or more electrons at any point in an atom or molecule, representable as a wave function.
